sampling_limits: Java execution sample shares exclude native GC/JIT and are not elapsed time shares.
Allocation sample weights estimate allocation churn, not retained heap.
run1.jfr is an overlapping snapshot, not independent samples.
The near-limit JFR subwindow alignment uses a second-precision command start and has approximately +/-1s uncertainty.
CPU load means are fractions of host capacity, not CPU-seconds; do not interpret them as single-core fractions.
GC CPU event sums measure GC records, while stop-the-world pause totals come from GarbageCollection.sumOfPauses.
Collapsed CPU stack shares sample all threads; they are not wall-time percentages. Disjoint categories prioritize bidi Java workers before GC keywords.
Resource CPU deltas are nearest 1-second process observations with endpoint errors shown, and include Java/JIT/GC/native CPU.
Minimum post-GC heap is a log observation, not a retained-object census. Young collections can leave still-uncollected old garbage.
No heap read, debugger, profiler attachment, or analyzer/Gradle execution was performed for this analysis.
GCCPUTime sums do not include all concurrent G1 worker CPU. Use saved native thread CPU deltas and collapsed native stacks for independent GC CPU evidence.
Current recording has no publication-batch width, distinct actual-input identity, match failure, or emitted-new-edge cardinality; speedup factors cannot be inferred.
FROZEN engine timeout means incomplete run-4 counters and output; only run-3 findings were accepted.

observations.finding: Run4 has expensive remaining handlers after most outer events complete.
observations.limit: Outer event completion does not count inner publication/candidate/transfer work. Long handlers finish during the interval, so this does not prove an infinite loop.

observations.finding: The early and late CPU profiles show different run4 work.
observations.limit: These are inclusive all-thread CPU sample shares, not wall-time attribution or candidate counts.

observations.finding: Current-demand lookup and saved-summary replay have distinct selected policies.
observations.limit: Saved replay precedes current-demand gating and runs on every offer by contract. Current notification coalescing alone does not remove native replay work.

observations.finding: Entry-key growth is small relative to offered initial candidates.
observations.limit: Existing initial keys can still produce new method/summary conclusions; this ratio is not the redundant-work percentage.

observations.finding: The run4 timeout is accompanied by allocation churn, not observed heap exhaustion.
observations.limit: No heap census was performed. Allocation sample weights measure cumulative allocation, and young post-GC heap is not exact retained size.

observations.finding: Current data does not establish static-versus-nonstatic dominance or a speedup multiplier.
observations.evidence: CPU/JFR stacks identify code paths, not fact values, exact callee keys, complete publication headers or duplicate actual-input identities.
observations.limit: Measure P/H for batch coalescing and S/U for equal-input factoring before predicting a factor-of-two reduction.

design_candidates.candidate: Coalesce compatible fresh AP publications inside the existing detached batch.
design_candidates.before: for each fresh delta: scan matching stored input members, match, apply, resume.
design_candidates.after: after the unchanged storage admission and FLOW-backed normalization: union fresh deltas by complete premise and compatible Facts.groupKey, then scan/match/apply packed deltas.
design_candidates.example: I→ret.a.$/T D, I→ret.b.$/T D, I→ret.c.$/T D with equal headers become one packed conclusion; all three paths remain.
design_candidates.required_proofs: Compatible packed matching/transfer/C5/cleanup distribute over union; same full premise, header and per-mark protection upgrade semantics remain; physical source/sink observations unchanged. Newly admitted subscriptions must still replay the current summary storage when a packed delivery uses one captured candidate snapshot.
design_candidates.required_measurement: P fresh publications per detached batch, H distinct full-premise/header groups, actual candidate scans/matches/application calls and fresh output memberships. No factor-of-two claim without measured P/H.

design_candidates.candidate: Factor pure selection of an identical actual input across full caller originals.
design_candidates.before: For each retained full CallerRef, run satisfying(actual,premise,mode), apply summary, restore caller context and resume.
design_candidates.after: Run pure selection once per complete actual+protection identity in the same publication/member/mode scope; retain existing per-CallerRef application and resume. A later phase may prepare immutable summary transfer parts once, with per-origin cycle protection after fanout.
design_candidates.example: Two caller originals P1 and P2 both submit local x.$/T to the same callee. Select x/T once; still emit both P1→result and P2→result.
design_candidates.required_proofs: Actual MAY/layer/E/mx/tail and protection remain exact. Caller full ND premise, cycle protection, source-summary Target discharge and suffix binding stay per-ref. TaintTree equality excludes protection, so plain Facts equality is not a valid complete key.
design_candidates.required_measurement: S candidate refs per publication/member and U distinct complete actual-input identities; successes, per-ref outputs and fresh storage admissions. No fixed improvement claim without S/U.

design_candidates.candidate: Assess the native persisted replay lane separately.
design_candidates.reason: Run4 replays saved summaries on every original offer before current-demand gating. Coalescing current notifications does not directly remove this selected behavior.
design_candidates.required_measurement: Native per-offer candidate counts, equal-input opportunities, source/normal Target dispatch and output deduplication. Do not silently restore fresh-only replay or add an input-history store.
